citeAs: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images. Technical Report, University of Toronto.
creator: Alex Krizhevsky (University of Toronto / Canadian Institute for Advanced Research)
description: CIFAR-100 is a labeled subset of the 80 million tiny images dataset, consisting of 600 images in each of 100 non-overlapping classes (60,000 images total). The 100 classes are organized into 20 superclasses of five classes each, and are mutually exclusive with the CIFAR-10 classes. Images are 32x32 colour images collected from the web.
name: CIFAR-100
rai:annotatorDemographics: Student labelers (paid students); no further demographic details provided
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Every label submitted by the labelers was personally verified by the authors. The labeling criteria specified that false positives (incorrectly included images) are worse than false negatives (incorrectly excluded images), biasing toward higher precision.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom in-house labeling task performed by paid students
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Students were paid a fixed sum per hour to label images. Each labeler was given a class and asked to examine all images found with that class as the search term, plus images found with hyponyms of the main search term (as defined by WordNet). Labelers were instructed to reject images not belonging to their assigned class. Criteria for inclusion: (1) the class name should be high on the list of likely answers to "What is in this picture?"; (2) the image should be photo-realistic (line drawings rejected); (3) the image should contain only one prominent instance of the object; (4) the object may be partially occluded or seen from an unusual viewpoint as long as its identity is clear. The authors personally verified every label submitted. Duplicate images were removed using L2 norm comparison with a threshold liberal enough to capture re-saved JPEGs.
rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from the 80 million tiny images dataset (assembled by colleagues at MIT and NYU by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in WordNet using search engines including Google, Flickr, and Altavista). Students were paid to label a subset: each labeler was given a class and asked to examine all images found with that class as the search term, as well as images found with hyponyms of the main search term (as defined by WordNet). Labelers were instructed to reject images that did not belong to their assigned class based on defined criteria. Every label submitted by labelers was personally verified by the authors. Duplicate images were removed by comparing images with the L2 norm.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data is the 80 million tiny images dataset, which contains 80 million colour images downscaled to 32x32 pixels, spread across 79,000 search terms. Images were collected by searching the web for every non-abstract English noun in WordNet using Google, Flickr, and Altavista, keeping roughly the first 3000 results per search term. Each image comes with a noisy label (the search term used to find it).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images from the 80 million tiny images dataset were already downscaled to 32x32 pixels. Perfect duplicates and images with an excessively large portion of white pixels were removed from the source dataset. For the labeled subset, duplicate images were removed by comparing images with the L2 norm using a rejection threshold liberal enough to capture not just perfect duplicates but also re-saved JPEGs. The dataset was divided into training and test sets, with the training set receiving a randomly-selected 5000 images from each class (for CIFAR-10; CIFAR-100 methodology was identical).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables research in object recognition and deep learning, contributing to advances in computer vision. The CIFAR-100 classes include images of people (baby, boy, girl, man, woman) collected from the web.
rai:dataUseCases: Object recognition and classification experiments; training and evaluating supervised and semi-supervised machine learning models; pre-training generative models (RBMs, DBNs) for feature learning; benchmark for image classification algorithms.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images of people (classes: baby, boy, girl, man, woman) collected from the web via image search engines. No explicit discussion of privacy or consent for individuals depicted.

null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described for the CIFAR-100 dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection manipulation protocol (augmentation, balancing, resampling) is described for the CIFAR-100 dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described for CIFAR-100.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine/ML annotation tools are described for the CIFAR-100 labeling pipeline; labeling was done manually by paid students.
